chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Rabi' al-Asamm, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had a wife in al-ʿIrāq, then committed fornication in al-Ḥijāz. So he said: “He is given the hadd punishment of the adulterer: one hundred lashes, and he is not stoned.”

I said: “Then if he is with her in one town, but he is confined in prison and unable to go out to her, and she cannot enter upon him—what do you think if he commits zina in prison?” He said: “He is in the position of one absent from his family; he is lashed one hundred times.”

key_terms.الْغَائِبِ عَنْ أَهْلِهِ: one absent from his family, used here as a legal comparison
key_terms.حَدَّ الزَّانِي: the fixed legal punishment for zina
key_terms.فُجُورًا: sexual immorality or illicit sexual conduct in this context
key_terms.مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ: one hundred lashes as the prescribed hadd here

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for zina if a married man is away from his wife or unable to reach her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on zina in the case of a man who has a wife but is effectively separated from access to her. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that when he is absent from his wife, or prevented from reaching her as in imprisonment, he is treated like one away from his family and receives one hundred lashes rather than rajm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5036 - It is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Rabi' Al-Asam, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who had a wife in Iraq but committed adultery in the Hijaz.
Imam (as) said: "He will be punished with one hundred lashes as the punishment for adultery but will not be stoned."

I asked: "What if he and his wife were in the same city, but he was imprisoned and unable to go to her, nor could she visit him, and he committed adultery in prison?"
Imam (as) replied: "He is like one who is absent from his family and will be lashed one hundred times."
